{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Brazil|Brazilian Cuisine]]

'''Farofa''' is a typical Brazilian dish made of toasted manioc flour. It's usually served as a side dish along with [[Cookbook:Feijoada|feijoada]] or grilled meat.

== Ingredients ==

* 1-2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]], preferably [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]].
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves, [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* A few pieces of [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] processed fatty [[Cookbook:Meat and Poultry|meat]] (typically [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]])
* 2 [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], chopped
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Manioc Flour|manioc (cassava) flour]] or premade farofa mix
* 1–2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Tempero Baiano|tempero baiano]] (see notes)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Cilantro|Cilantro]] to taste, chopped (optional)

== Procedure ==

# Heat a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium heat. Add the meat and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] for a minute or so. Depending on how much fat is released from it, add up to 1 tbsp of the oil or butter, enough to fry the garlic and onions.
# Add the garlic, and stir for a minute or so, making sure not to let it burn.
# Add the onion and seasonings, and cook for about another minute.
# Add the flour and any additional ingredients. Stir well and continue toasting for a couple minutes more. If using premade farofa mix, stir until the extra ingredients are well-done. If using raw cassava flour, slowly add the remaining butter or oil and stir until toasted and golden.
# Turn off the heat, and add chopped cilantro if desired. Serve hot to warm.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Additional ingredients may be added for taste and texture. Common additions are green [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]], fried [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantains]], ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], dry [[Cookbook:Textured Vegetable Protein|textured vegetable protein]] and onion flakes.
* Tempero baiano (see notes) is a Brazilian spice mix based on [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]], [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]], [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]] and [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]. If you don't have it, you can add the individual components to taste.
* Manioc flour or premade farofa mix may already be salted, so taste when adding more salt.
* Coarse corn flour in flakes can be used as a substitute for the cassava flour.
